pins.title: How Heavy Should a Weighted Blanket Be? The 10% Rule and a Quick Weight Chart
pins.subtitle: Pick the right weight the first time
pins.description: Not sure which weighted blanket weight to buy? The most common guideline is roughly 10% of your body weight, give or take a pound or two. This guide has a simple chart by body weight, plus what couples usually do instead of one oversized blanket (size for the lighter partner, or get two). Save it for when you shop. #weightedblanket #sleepbetter #bedroomideas #sleeptips #anxietyrelief #cozybedroom

pins.title: Hot Sleeper? Why Most People Quit Their Weighted Blanket (and the Fabric That Fixes It)
pins.subtitle: Cotton weave vs minky vs glass beads
pins.description: Weighted blankets get abandoned more often for heat than for weight. A breathable cotton or cooling weave suits hot sleepers and warm rooms; minky plush feels softer but traps more heat; glass bead fill spreads weight more evenly than plastic pellets. Read the material breakdown before you buy. #weightedblanket #hotsleeper #coolingbedding #sleeptips #bedroomideas #sleepbetter

pins.title: Do Weighted Blankets Help With Racing Thoughts at Bedtime? What the Research Says
pins.subtitle: Where they help, and where they don't
pins.description: Weighted blankets rely on deep pressure stimulation, which some research links to a calmer nervous system response. Several small studies found modest improvements in self-reported sleep quality and anxiety, but they are not a treatment for insomnia caused by a medical condition and are not for young children. An honest look at who they tend to help. Not medical advice. #weightedblanket #sleepanxiety #bedtimeroutine #sleepbetter #calmnight #wellnesstips
